universities.name: Catolica Medical School, Universidade Catolica Portuguesa
universities.summary: Catolica Medical School at Universidade Catolica Portuguesa runs a direct-entry, six-year Integrated Master in Medicine on its Sintra Campus near Lisbon. The programme is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools, accredited by Portugal's A3ES (a WFME-recognized agency), and its graduates become ECFMG-certification eligible from 2027, the year its first cohort graduates.
universities.campusLifestyle: International students join a Problem-Based-Learning curriculum modeled on Maastricht University's method, in small tutorial groups, on the university's dedicated Sintra Campus near Tagus Park, with a free shuttle service connecting to Lisbon.
universities.cityProfile: Sintra sits in the Greater Lisbon area, a short shuttle ride from Portugal's capital, giving students access to Lisbon's teaching hospitals and international-student community while based on a purpose-built campus.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year, 360-ECTS Integrated Master in Medicine runs Years 1-2 as pre-clinical functional-integration modules, Year 3 as an introduction to clinical practice, Years 4-5 as clinical rotations across Internal Medicine, Surgery, Family Medicine, Women and Child Health and Neurosciences, and Year 6 as supervised healthcare-participation and research internships, with clinical teaching at Hospital da Luz Lisboa, Hospital Beatriz Angelo, and other Grupo Luz Saude and public-health-service facilities.
universities.hostelOverview: The university guarantees supported accommodation specifically when a clinical rotation placement is more than 40km from the Sintra campus; no confirmed general on-campus dormitory for the medical programme was found, and typical off-campus housing costs in the Lisbon/Sintra area were not independently sourced. A general-purpose Female University Residence exists in Lisbon for the wider Universidade Catolica Portuguesa student body. Applicants should confirm current housing options directly with the university's International Mobility and Relations Office.
universities.dietarySupport: Subsidised canteen meals are available to students, per the university's own scholarships and support page.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found during research.
universities.studentSupport: International applicants use a dedicated Non-EU International Students admissions track, apply through the university's Fenix online platform, and can contact the Faculty's International Mobility and Relations Office for further guidance.
whyChoose: Listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools (FAIMER School ID F0007778), with the WDOMS record confirming direct-entry (prerequisite: completed secondary education, no prior degree required).
Accredited by Portugal's Agencia de Avaliacao e Acreditacao do Ensino Superior (A3ES), a WFME-recognized agency, for a full 6-year accreditation term published 9 September 2020.
Graduates become eligible to apply for ECFMG Certification from 2027, the year the first cohort graduates.
Pre-clinical years (1-3) are taught in English, with a modern Problem-Based-Learning curriculum modeled on Maastricht University's method and a notably favorable student-to-clinical-teacher ratio.
A structured, transparent international-applicant admissions process with a published fee schedule, calendar and dedicated Mini Multiple Interview evaluation.
thingsToConsider: The clinical years (4-6) carry an official university caveat that the clinical component is delivered in Portuguese, distinct from the confirmed English-medium pre-clinical years -- functional Portuguese will likely be needed for clinical-year patient contact.

Indian secondary qualifications (CBSE/ISC and similar) are not on the university's published list of recognized equivalent international exams; Indian applicants would likely need to sit the university's own in-person entrance exams in Biology, Physics and Chemistry, and Mathematics, conducted in English at the Sintra campus.
Total annual cost is substantial: EUR 24,350/year tuition plus a EUR 1,710 first-year (EUR 1,680 later years) enrollment/registration fee and a one-time EUR 430 application fee.

The university's own pages give two different English-proficiency minimums (CEFR C1 on one page, CEFR B2 with specific accepted test scores on more recently updated application pages) -- an unresolved inconsistency in the university's own materials; confirm the current requirement directly before applying.
Only 9 places are available for the international (non-EU) admissions track for the 2026/27 cycle, making this a small, competitive cohort.
bestFitFor: Students seeking a newer, WFME-recognized, English-medium (pre-clinical) direct-entry medical degree with a modern Problem-Based-Learning curriculum.
Applicants comfortable preparing for in-person entrance exams and a Mini Multiple Interview conducted in English at the Sintra campus.
Families able to budget for a European private-university fee level and who are comfortable with developing functional Portuguese ahead of clinical-year rotations.

faq.question: Is the Integrated Master in Medicine direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. The WHO World Directory of Medical Schools confirms admission follows completion of secondary education, with no prior university degree required.

faq.question: Is the whole programme taught in English?
faq.answer: Pre-clinical years (1-3) are confirmed English-medium by multiple official sources. The university's own programme overview states the clinical component (Years 4-6) is delivered in Portuguese, so functional Portuguese will likely be needed for clinical-year patient contact.

faq.question: Can Indian students apply directly with their 12th-grade marks?
faq.answer: Indian secondary qualifications are not on the university's published list of recognized equivalent exams (which includes Cambridge AICE, IB, European Baccalaureate, AP and Brazil's ENEM). Indian applicants would likely need to sit the university's own in-person entrance exams in Biology, Physics and Chemistry, and Mathematics, conducted in English.

faq.question: What English-proficiency score is required?
faq.answer: The university's more recently updated application pages state a minimum CEFR B2 (IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72, or equivalent), though an older summary page states CEFR C1 -- this inconsistency is unresolved on the official site, so confirm the current requirement directly with the university.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: EUR 24,350 per year for international students (EUR 2,435/month over 10 instalments), confirmed current for the 2026/27 academic year, plus a one-time EUR 430 application fee and a EUR 1,710 first-year (EUR 1,680 later years) enrollment/registration fee.

faq.question: Are scholarships available?
faq.answer: The university publishes merit-based and need-based annual scholarships, including full-tuition Study Grants, assessed by its Social Responsibility Office based on application grade and household economic situation. Exact eligibility terms and amounts specifically for international applicants were not itemized separately from domestic applicants on the official page.

faq.question: When is the application deadline and intake for 2026/27?
faq.answer: The Non-EU international-applicant track runs a single application window from 8 July to 31 August 2026, with results published 7 September 2026 and classes beginning 8 September 2026. Only 9 places are available on this track.

faq.question: Is there an interview as part of admissions?
faq.answer: Yes. In addition to a motivation letter/portfolio, applicants must attend a mandatory in-person Mini Multiple Interview at the Sintra campus, conducted in English.

faq.question: Can this degree be used to practice medicine outside Portugal?
faq.answer: Graduates become eligible to apply for ECFMG Certification from 2027. The degree is expected to fall under Portugal's EU Directive 2005/36/EC automatic-recognition framework for medical qualifications, though the exact current Annex V listing of this specific post-Bologna degree title was not independently confirmed during research. For India specifically, graduates would need to separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission screening requirements; this was not verified against an NMC source, and no graduates of this programme exist yet to test that pathway.

ctas.label: Build my cost and funding plan

fee.notes: Officially published 2026/27 tuition: EUR 24,350/year (EUR 2,435/month over 10 monthly instalments) for international students, confirmed on the university's own scholarships-and-fees page. A separate one-time EUR 430 non-refundable application fee and a EUR 1,710 first-year (EUR 1,680 later years) annual enrollment/registration fee also apply. Total is calculated as the annual tuition figure times 6 years -- not published as a lump sum, and does not include the application/enrollment fees. The university explicitly states fee values are published annually and may change in subsequent academic years.

eligibleAudiences: Non-EU international applicants who have completed secondary education, subject to entrance-exam and English-proficiency requirements
restrictions: Applicants whose secondary-school system is not on the university's recognized equivalency list (which excludes India) must sit the university's own in-person entrance exams in Biology, Physics and Chemistry, and Mathematics
Minimum English-proficiency certificate required (CEFR B2 per the most recently updated application pages; an older summary page states C1, an unresolved inconsistency)
Only 9 places available on the international (non-EU) admissions track for 2026/27
audienceEligibility.notes: Admission also requires a motivation letter/portfolio and a mandatory in-person Mini Multiple Interview at the Sintra campus, conducted in English.

admissionsContent.overview: Non-EU international applicants apply online via the university's Fenix platform, submit a motivation letter/portfolio, sit entrance exams if their home-country qualification is not on the recognized equivalency list, and attend a mandatory in-person Mini Multiple Interview at the Sintra campus before results are published.

eligibility.intro: Admission requires a secondary-school qualification (or recognized equivalent), qualifying entrance-exam scores, and English-proficiency proof.
items: Secondary-school diploma with DGES equivalence certification for foreign qualifications
Entrance exams in Biology/Geology, Physics/Chemistry and Mathematics (min. 140/200 each) -- required for applicants whose system, including India, is not on the equivalency list
Minimum CEFR B2 English-proficiency certificate (per the most current application pages)

applicationSteps: Create an online account and apply via the university's Fenix platform (8 July-31 August 2026)
Submit an online motivation letter/portfolio within 48 hours of application validation
Sit the university's in-person entrance exams if applicable, and submit final grades/documents
Attend the mandatory in-person Mini Multiple Interview at the Sintra campus (3 September 2026)
Await published results (7 September 2026) and complete registration (7-9 September 2026)
